title: Cheesy Potato Gratin
summary: Thinly sliced potatoes are simmered in a garlic- and thyme-infused cream, layered with alpine-style cheese and Parmesan, then baked until bubbling and deep golden on top.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
floury potatoes (such as russet or Maris Piper), peeled
Parmesan or a vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated

steps.title: Infuse the cream
steps.text: Bring the cream, milk, garlic, shallots, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper to the boil in a saucepan, then take off the heat, cover and leave to steep for 30-60 minutes. This slow infusion draws flavour from the garlic, shallot and thyme into the liquid without needing to simmer it down.

steps.title: Strain and slice
steps.text: Return the liquid to the boil, then strain it through a fine sieve into a large heatproof bowl, discarding the solids. Slice the potatoes 1.5-2 mm thick straight into the hot liquid, stirring so every slice is coated; skip rinsing them, since the starch on their surface is what thickens the sauce as it bakes.

steps.title: Preheat and mix cheeses
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, and butter the baking dish. Mix the grated alpine-style cheese and Parmesan together, keeping the final third aside for the top layer.

steps.title: Layer the gratin
steps.text: Layer the potato slices in the dish, scattering cheese between each layer and reserving the last portion for the top. Pour over the remaining infused liquid until it just reaches the top layer of potatoes. Building it in layers lets the cheese melt evenly through the gratin instead of pooling at the base.

steps.title: Bake covered, then open
steps.text: Cover with foil and bake on a tray for 45 minutes, then remove the foil, scatter over the remaining cheese and bake for a further 30-40 minutes. It's ready when a knife slides through with no resistance and the top is deep golden; the foil traps steam early on to cook the potatoes through before the top is left bare to brown.

steps.title: Rest before cutting
steps.text: Let the gratin rest for 15 minutes before cutting into it. As it cools slightly, the starchy cream firms up and sets, so the layers hold together on the plate instead of slipping apart.

tips: Slice the potatoes evenly, ideally with a mandoline, so they cook at the same rate and the layers sit flush.
A common mistake is rinsing the sliced potatoes - this washes away the starch that thickens the sauce, leaving it thin and watery.
Use floury potatoes rather than waxy ones; they break down just enough to help the sauce cling.
Let the dish rest the full 15 minutes before cutting, or the slices will slump instead of holding their layers.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat portions in a low oven or microwave until piping hot throughout (74°C); this dish freezes well for up to 2 months, thawed overnight in the fridge before reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
